name: Autosomal Dominant Primary Microcephaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Microcephaly

criteria.description: Head circumference more than 3 standard deviations below the mean for age and sex
Mild to moderate intellectual disability without progressive neurological deterioration
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Brain MRI showing reduced brain volume without major structural abnormalities
Exclusion of metabolic or infectious causes of microcephaly

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of microcephaly, intellectual disability, and autosomal dominant family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of secondary causes of microcephaly.

imaging: Brain MRI showing reduced cerebral volume without major structural malformations
Normal or mildly simplified gyral pattern
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes associated with autosomal dominant primary microcephaly (e.g., ASPM, WDR62 mutations less common in dominant form)
Family segregation analysis confirming autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Normal growth parameters except head circumference

distinguishingFeatures: Often associated with structural brain abnormalities
History of prenatal infections or exposure

redFlags: Presence of major brain malformations on imaging
references: Woods CG, et al. Autosomal dominant primary microcephaly: clinical and genetic features. Am J Med Genet A. 2019.
Orphanet: Autosomal dominant primary microcephaly. ORPHA:2514.
